newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares mixed as Christmas nears.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares mixed as Christmas nears.

text.p: Leading Russian shares were mixed in afternoon trading on Wednesday with many foreign investors closing their books for Christmas, dealers said.
At 1345 GMT Rostelekom rose to $2.29 from $2.27 at Tuesday's close, Mosenergo was $0.965 after $0.966, Lenenergo fell to $0.350 from $0.387 and LUKoil edged up to $10.33 from $10.31.

"The market is practically not moving," said Alexander Pankov, a trader from CentreInvest Securities. "There are no sellers at current levels. It is a pity to sell now. Foreigners are getting ready for Christmas and closing their books."
He said there was only one big foreign order for UES that had been in the market for the last three days but had failed to raise the price.
UES was $0.0828 after $0.0825 at Tuesday's close.
Norilsk Nickel fell to $5.00 from $5.17, but Pankov said the share has a good support at $4.90-$4.95 bid price and said it would not fall any further.
He said Norilsk Nickel could double in price by next summer.
Samaraenergo was the gainer of the day with the price rising to $0.34 from $0.30.
However, Pankov said that there was big supply of regional power and telecommunications companies shares from the regions. These shares have been the hit of the market in recent months.

Victor Pitaleff, a trader from Renaissance Capital said investor interest was focused in leading shares, while second-tier and preferred share prices were overheated and buyers waited for them to fall.
Pankov forecast a rise in Tatneft shares after the 30-day period expires after which the company's shares could be converted into American Depositary Receipts.
Tatneft was not traded on Wednesday, but closed at $46.00 on December 11 when it was last traded.
The company has just completed placement of its American Depositary Shares. The issue was heavily oversubscribed, but Tatneft shares cannot be freely converted into ADS.
